cohort: This study involved 130 patients undergoing cesarean delivery under spinal anesthesia, divided into two groups receiving either bupivacaine or normal saline infiltration along the incision line.
finding: Local infiltration of bupivacaine significantly prolonged the pain-free interval, provided better pain relief for the first 6 hours post-operation, and reduced the need for systemic analgesics within the first 24 hours after cesarean delivery compared to normal saline.
